verdict.rationale: Zep documents first-party deletion controls. Deleting a user cascades to all of that user's threads and thread artifacts in one API call, explicitly framed for Right To Be Forgotten requests. Graph nodes and edges can also be deleted individually. However, the pack shows no configurable retention policy, such as TTLs, automatic expiry or retention windows, so the retention half of the story is unevidenced. missing for 10: configurable data retention periods/automatic expiry, independent or hands-on corroboration of deletion completeness.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: Deleting a User will delete all Threads and thread artifacts associated with that User with a single API call, making it easy to handle Right To Be Forgotten requests.
This single-operation approach makes it simple to handle Right To Be Forgotten (RTBF) requests and comply with privacy regulations.
Deleting a node will also delete all edges connected to that node.
